主要内容: The global fire protection materials for construction market is expected to grow from $3.81 billion in 2021 to $4.32 billion in 2022 at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13.4%. This growth is primarily attributed to companies resuming operations and adapting to the new normal while recovering from the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, which led to restrictive containment measures such as social distancing, remote working, and closure of commercial activities. The market is projected to reach $6.04 billion by 2026 at a CAGR of 8.7%. Fire protection materials include concrete, reinforcement steel, gypsum, cast iron, bricks, asbestos cement, timber, stone, glass, and others. The main types of fire protection materials are coatings, mortar, sealants, fillers, sheets or boards, spray, preformed devices, putty, cast-in devices, and others. North America was the largest region in the fire protection materials for construction market in 2021. Growing regulations on the mandatory use of fire safety materials are expected to positively impact the market's growth. Fire safety standards aim to reduce the fire-response of products and materials used in various living environments, including buildings and transportation. For instance, the Home Office introduced the new Fire Safety Bill in March 2020 to improve fire safety in buildings in England and Wales. The Fire Safety Act 2021 has been implemented as a law in the country. Key manufacturers are focusing on cutting-edge research and technological advancements to create improved fire protection materials that can withstand fire for a longer period and emit less smoke when burned. For example, in September 2020, CIN, a Portugal-based company, developed two new products, C-THERM S110 and C-THERM S111 FD, to protect steel structures from fire. The Fire Protection Materials For Construction Global Market Report 2022 highlights the importance of fire protection materials in enhancing structural safety during fires. Technologies such as those in the C-THERM range are designed to delay the collapse of structures for up to 150 minutes, thereby protecting both lives and property. In October 2020, API Group Inc., a US-based provider of specialty, safety, and industrial services, acquired SK FireSafety Group for $200 million. This acquisition is expected to support the growth and geographic expansion of API Group Inc.'s safety services and specialty services divisions. SK FireSafety Group B.V., a Netherlands-based company, specializes in providing fire protection products for businesses.
